title: Can a figure with four right angles have unequal opposite sides?
description: A base is drawn with an upright line at each end, and the top is joined across. The two uprights stay the same distance apart, so the top side comes out as long as the base. Keeko's doubt is that the top side can be shorter because the uprights lean in.
teaching_notes: One idea: a four-sided figure with four right angles has equal opposite sides, because two lines at ninety degrees to the same base never lean. Watch for students who think the uprights can lean and still make right angles.

video_script.why: A learner sees why four right angles force the opposite sides of a four-sided figure to be equal.
video_script.substitution: the book's own question about a four-sided figure with all angles ninety degrees
video_script.anchor: a four-sided figure with four right-angle marks, as in the book's question
video_script.wrong_answer: the top side can be shorter than the bottom side
video_script.wrong_move: leans the two upright lines inwards so that the top side comes out shorter than the base
video_script.payoff_line: The opposite sides must always be equal.

final_answer.value: No. A figure with all four angles 90° is a rectangle, so its opposite sides are equal
final_answer.spoken: no, the opposite sides must be equal

maths_rules: two lines each at 90° to the same base AB never lean, so they stay the same distance apart
the angles at D and C are 90°, so DC runs straight across and DC = AB
the same reasoning gives AD = BC
all angles 90° and opposite sides equal: the figure is a rectangle (R1 and R2)
video_script.design: One four-sided figure built step by step: base, two uprights, top. The uprights are drawn with equal gaps marked at two heights.

beats.on_screen: title card, then a four-sided figure with a right-angle mark at each of its four corners and a question mark between the two top corners

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the four-sided figure is drawn
marks.ask: the two opposite sides glow and a question mark appears

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about a four-sided figure.
<bookmark mark='angles'/>All four of its corners are right angles, which means ninety degrees.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Can the opposite sides, the sides that face each other, be unequal?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a straight base AB, and at A and B one upright line each, drawn at a right angle to the base and labelled perpendicular

marks.perp: the upright line at A is drawn with its right-angle mark and labelled perpendicular
marks.two: the second upright line at B is drawn

narration: <bookmark mark='line'/>Draw one side of the figure as a straight base.
<bookmark mark='perp'/>A line that meets the base at ninety degrees is called a perpendicular.
<bookmark mark='two'/>At each end of the base stands one perpendicular, so the figure has two upright sides.

beats.on_screen: Given: a 4-sided figure ABCD with all four angles 90°
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a four-sided figure in which all four angles are ninety degrees.

beats.on_screen: To find: can the opposite sides be unequal?

marks.find: the question is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find whether the opposite sides can be unequal.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: draw base AB; draw a perpendicular at A and at B (angle A = angle B = 90°)

marks.base: the base AB is drawn and the two uprights rise from A and B
marks.angles: the two right-angle marks at A and B light up

narration: <bookmark mark='base'/>Step one, draw the base eigh bee, and draw perpendiculars at eigh and bee.
<bookmark mark='angles'/>The angles at eigh and bee are ninety degrees, so both lines stand straight up.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: both lines make 90° with AB, so neither leans; the gap between them is the same at every height

marks.apart: the two uprights are drawn without a lean
marks.gap: equal double arrows appear between them at two heights

narration: <bookmark mark='apart'/>Step two, neither perpendicular leans, because each makes ninety degrees with the base.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>The two lines stay the same distance apart all the way up.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: join the tops D and C; angle D = angle C = 90°, so DC runs straight across and DC is as long as AB

marks.top: the tops D and C are joined
marks.across: the right-angle marks at D and C light up
marks.same: a double arrow shows DC and AB are the same length

narration: <bookmark mark='top'/>Step three, join the tops dee and cee.
<bookmark mark='across'/>The angles at dee and cee are ninety degrees as well, so dee cee runs straight across.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Dee cee crosses the same gap as eigh bee, so dee cee is as long as eigh bee.

beats.on_screen: Answer: No. The figure is a rectangle, so opposite sides are equal
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The opposite sides must always be equal.
<bookmark mark='no'/>The answer is no, and the figure is a rectangle.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the finished figure
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: the two uprights drawn leaning inwards, with a shorter top side; the leaning angles are marked less than a right angle, then the picture is struck out

marks.doubt: the leaning uprights and the short top side appear
marks.fix: the leaning angles light up as not ninety degrees, and the picture is struck out
marks.both: both uprights are redrawn straight and the top side matches the base

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the top side can be shorter than the bottom side. Keeko says the upright lines can lean in.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But a line that leans in does not make ninety degrees with the base.
<bookmark mark='both'/>Both uprights make ninety degrees, so neither can lean, and the top side matches the bottom side.
